49: ## Execution modes and local run
50: 
51: All main classes require distinct `SCHOLARCHAIN_API_KEY_SHA256` and
52: `SCHOLARCHAIN_INTERNAL_TOKEN_SHA256`; there are no fallback credentials. Invalid/missing
53: configuration exits **2**, including malformed worker configuration before a listener starts.
54: Default `SCHOLARCHAIN_SERVICE_MODE=unconfigured` keeps liveness 200 and readiness 503 and
55: refuses query work. It never silently selects synthetic data as a production fallback.
56: 
57: Set `SCHOLARCHAIN_SERVICE_MODE=offline-synthetic` to explicitly run the declared Phase 9 G1
58: fixture. This mode creates only fake stores and a scripted model; no AWS SDK/provider client
59: or credentials are discovered. Its supported question is exactly:
60: 
61: ```json
62: {"question":"Synthetic fixture: publication count for A","output":{"includeScores":false}}
63: ```
64: 
65: A real `RuntimeAnswerWorkflow` retrieves fixture evidence, a scripted proposal copies its
66: publication-count value, `ClaimVerificationAgent` checks it, and the audit is persisted.
67: Other questions or mismatched structured constraints return typed 422 rather than invented
68: answers. All fixture identities and overlays are synthetic, as declared in `RuntimeOfflineFixture`.
69: The independently owned test fixture supplies separate hand-derived expected values.
70: 
71: Configure `SCHOLARCHAIN_GRAPH_BASE_URI` and `SCHOLARCHAIN_SEMANTIC_BASE_URI` together on
72: query-api to use independently running service artifacts. These HTTP(S) base URLs are runtime
73: inputs; URI user-info is forbidden. Supply `SCHOLARCHAIN_INTERNAL_TOKEN` through deployment
74: secret injection for outgoing calls and ensure its hash matches the internal-token hash.
75: The raw token is never logged, returned or committed. In that composition query execution
76: reads actual remote graph metric records and actual remote semantic hits, and graph exploration
77: is proxied to the graph artifact. Both dependency readiness checks must succeed for readiness
78: 200. No request is sent to an AWS or paid model endpoint by these entrypoints.
79: 
80: Graph-service and semantic-service in offline mode use immutable fake graph/vector ports.
81: The semantic index starts empty and returns truthful empty hits; it never invents context.
82: Embedding-worker starts a bounded loop over an empty fake queue with a real
83: `ManifestEmbeddingProcessor`/`EmbeddingManifestRunner`; injection tests enqueue actual bounded
84: synthetic work. Live stores, SQS URLs, model clients and deployment lifecycle remain later
85: approved composition inputs. Offline mode is not a live production adapter configuration.

230: ## Configuration and verification
231: 
232: `ServiceConfig.fromEnvironment` externalizes application limits with prefix `SCHOLARCHAIN_`:
233: 
234: | Suffix | Default / rationale |
235: | --- | --- |
236: | API_KEY_SHA256, INTERNAL_TOKEN_SHA256 | Required distinct SHA-256 hashes; no default credentials |
237: | HTTP_HOST, HTTP_PORT | 127.0.0.1, 8080; explicit container bind |
238: | SYNCHRONOUS_DEADLINE_MS, WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MS | 15000, 60000; independent finite wait/execution bounds |
239: | MAX_WORKFLOW_RETRIES | 2; bounded job retries |
240: | WORKER_THREADS, QUEUE_CAPACITY | 4, 64; bounded execution and backlog |
241: | MAX_REQUEST_BYTES, MAX_RESULT_BYTES | 65536, 131072; bounded wire/result memory |
242: | MAX_QUESTION_CHARS | 8192 |
243: | MAX_GRAPH_LIMIT, MAX_VECTOR_LIMIT, MAX_PATH_DEPTH | 100, 50, 6; runtime query caps distinct from graph exploration caps |
244: | MAX_FILTER_ITEMS, MAX_FILTER_CHARS | 100, 512 |
245: | MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CHARS | 256 before hashing |
246: | DOWNSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS, DOWNSTREAM_MAX_ATTEMPTS | 5000, 3 per-read attempt |
247: | GRAPH_DEADLINE_RESERVE_PERCENT | 25; response headroom for graph requests, 1–99 |
248: | GRAPH_TIMEOUT_MS | 5000; positive declared graph work cap before proxy clamp |
249: | BREAKER_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, BREAKER_RESET_MS | 3, 30000 |
250: | SESSION_CAS_ATTEMPTS, SESSION_POLL_MS | 8, 50; tune poll interval upward for remote stores |
251: | REQUEST_READ_TIMEOUT_MS | 5000 socket inactivity bound, not an aggregate upload deadline |
252: 
253: Additional bootstrap graph prefix `SCHOLARCHAIN_GRAPH_`: `DIRECTION=both`,
254: `DEFAULT_DEPTH=1`, `MAX_DEPTH=3`, `DEFAULT_LIMIT=50`, `MAX_LIMIT=200`, `TIMEOUT_MS=5000`,
255: `DEFAULT_WINDOW=all-years`, `MAX_SCANNED_EDGES=10000`, `MAX_VISITED_NODES=2000`,
256: `MAX_CURSOR_CHARS=4096`, and `CURSOR_KEY` (random per-process unless injected).
257: Worker prefix `SCHOLARCHAIN_WORKER_`: `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`, `BATCH_SIZE=1`, `POLL_MS=1000`.
258: Semantic injection config defaults top-K 50, question chars 8192, body bytes 65536,
259: filter count 16 and timeout 5000 ms. All caps are configured application bounds, not measured

1: # EMR Spark compatibility research for 6A
2: 
3: Owner: `infra-engineer`, native task `/root/infra_6a` (read-only research; no AWS account calls). This memo records published runtime facts and candidate investigations. It is not deployment approval or a successful EMR run.
4: 
5: ## Published runtime versions
6: 
7: The [AWS EMR 7.x application version table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-release-app-versions-7.x.html) lists Spark 3.5.x releases with Scala 2.12: EMR 7.0–7.2 use Scala 2.12.17; EMR 7.3–7.14 use Scala 2.12.18. EMR 7.8 has Spark 3.5.4-amzn-0 and Scala 2.12.18. The [EMR 7.8 release page](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-780-release.html) lists Corretto 17 as Spark's default Java runtime. The [EMR 7.0](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-700-release.html) and [7.14](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-7140-release.html) pages also list the supported Java runtimes for their releases.
8: 
9: Repository `project/Versions.scala` pins Scala 3.3.4 and Spark 3.5.4; `project/Dependencies.scala` requests `spark-sql_2.13` on the Provided classpath. [Scala's binary compatibility guide](https://docs.scala-lang.org/overviews/core/binary-compatibility-of-scala-releases.html) describes Scala 3 interoperability with Scala 2.13 libraries, not Scala 2.12 libraries. [Spark's 3.5 documentation](https://spark.apache.org/docs/3.5.2/) says the application must use the same Scala binary version as Spark. Therefore stock EMR 7.x is **not demonstrated binary compatible** with this job. The use of Java/DataFrame entry points narrows the API surface but does not establish runtime linkage. No EMR job was run.
10: 
11: ## Fallbacks to investigate if a live EMR run is required
12: 
13: | Candidate | Published support and validation needed | Cost and operational factors |
14: |---|---|---|
15: | EMR Serverless custom image | [AWS custom image guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/EMR-Serverless-UserGuide/application-custom-image.html) requires a release-matched base and warns that changing binaries or JARs may prevent startup. A Scala-2.13 Spark replacement needs a feasibility proof. | Worker CPU, memory and storage are billed while active, including image startup. Image maintenance and compatibility testing are additional work. |
16: | EMR on EKS custom image | [Custom image steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/EMR-on-EKS-DevelopmentGuide/docker-custom-images-steps.html) and [considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/EMR-on-EKS-DevelopmentGuide/docker-custom-images-considerations.html) allow customization, but do not guarantee a Scala-2.13 Spark swap. | EKS cluster, worker compute and storage, plus EMR job charges; Kubernetes and image patching add operational work. |
17: | EMR on EC2 with separate Spark distribution | [EMR software planning guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-software.html) permits bootstrap installation of custom software. A distinct Spark 3.5.x/Scala-2.13 distribution would need scheduler, classpath, connector and patch validation. | EMR and EC2/EBS charges accrue while the cluster runs; custom distribution upkeep and integration are project responsibilities. |
18: 
19: The cost dimensions are described by [Amazon EMR pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/emr/pricing/) and [Amazon EKS pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/eks/pricing/). No dollar estimates or regional availability claims were made. A separate Scala-2.12 Spark layer behind a Java boundary is another possible architecture change, but it is an inference and was not validated. The user requested comparison, not a fallback selection. Any live test remains behind the later human budget and deployment gate.
20: 
21: ## Scala 2.13 patch alignment for a custom Spark runtime — 6A repair round 1
22: 
23: Read-only `infra-engineer` research found that the [upstream Spark 3.5.4 Scala-2.13 build profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/spark/v3.5.4/pom.xml#L3625-L3630) pins Scala **2.13.8**. The existing local job JAR's `library.properties`, read with `unzip -p modules/spark/target/spark-job_3-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar library.properties`, reports `version.number=2.13.14`; `project/Versions.scala` pins `scala-reflect` 2.13.14. These are upstream-build and local-package observations, **not** an inventory of a proposed custom EMR image or distribution.
24: 
25: The [Scala binary compatibility policy](https://docs.scala-lang.org/overviews/core/binary-compatibility-of-scala-releases.html) states that Scala 2.13 patch releases through 2.13.18 retain both backward and forward binary compatibility, subject to exceptions for experimental or internal APIs and generated code. [Scala 3 interoperability guidance](https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/guides/migration/interoperability.html) explains its use of the Scala 2.13 standard library. Thus the 2.13.8-versus-2.13.14 patch difference alone does **not** establish a linkage failure. The stock EMR Scala **2.12 versus 2.13** mismatch remains the primary known incompatibility.
26: 
27: Before any 6H live run, after a human selects and authorizes a bounded fallback, inventory the exact Spark, `scala-library`, `scala-reflect`, `scala3-library` and Scala module JAR versions on **both driver and executors**. Compare them with the packaged job JAR and record effective class origins so duplicate Scala classes are visible. The preferred alignment is a coherent Spark 3.5.4 `_2.13` distribution with its tested Scala patch level and a job package built and verified against that same level; if the job must retain 2.13.14 while the selected distribution uses another 2.13 patch, require a documented compatibility proof on that exact pair. Then run a bounded startup and representative DataFrame/Parquet task and compare its rows with the local 6G result. Retain class origins, versions, logs, and any linkage or serialization error. Spark's `spark.driver.userClassPathFirst` and `spark.executor.userClassPathFirst` default to false and are marked experimental in the [Spark 3.5 configuration reference](https://spark.apache.org/docs/3.5.7/configuration.html#runtime-environment); changing classpath precedence is a contingency to test, not an assumed fix. Shading `scala.*` is likewise an unvalidated and risky inference because Spark and the job exchange Scala types. No custom runtime was selected or executed in this repair round.

16: RUN case "$MAIN_CLASS" in \
17:     edu.uic.cs441.scholarchain.services.QueryApiMain|\
18:     edu.uic.cs441.scholarchain.services.GraphServiceMain|\
19:     edu.uic.cs441.scholarchain.services.SemanticServiceMain|\
20:     edu.uic.cs441.scholarchain.services.EmbeddingWorkerMain) ;; \
21:     *) echo "Unsupported service main class" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
22:     esac
23: ENV SCHOLARCHAIN_MAIN_CLASS=${MAIN_CLASS}
24:

27: ENTRYPOINT ["sh", "-c", "exec java -cp '/app/services.jar:/app/lib/*' \"$SCHOLARCHAIN_MAIN_CLASS\" \"$@\"", "scholarchain"]

155: Default graph exploration is `direction=both`, depth 1 (maximum 3), limit 50 (maximum 200),
156: edge types from `COAUTHORED_WITH,AUTHORED,HAS_TOPIC,AFFILIATED_WITH,PUBLISHED_IN`, and timeout
157: 5000 ms. Complete expansion is bounded by edge/node scan caps and the aggregate requested
158: deadline, including blocking adapter calls. Stable BFS order determines pages. Signed opaque
159: cursors bind node, snapshot, direction, depth, edge filters, window, page limit and timeout.
160: Changing any binding or tampering rejects the cursor. Use a stable secret cursor key across
161: replicas; a per-process random key intentionally invalidates old cursors after restart.
162: Path results use shortest bounded BFS and never exceed the requested hop cap. Truncated
